Title: Questions about the game from a new player.

Messages.Author: cool....@gmail.com
Messages.Body:
Hello,
I have some questions about the game mechanics and rules i don't seem
to understand, i hope someone here could help me out because i can't
seem to find help anywhere else.
I've got a few questions which follows:

Action modifier cards: will using them Tap a minion?
Are they a one turn card which gets burned after using or are they
permanent to the assigned minion?
The whole inactive region was also a little confusing, how much blood
counts does it cost to bring a vampire from your crypt? how much does
it cost to bring a vampire into the active region and how much does it
cost to move him back to the inactive region?
Can you move blood counts from an active vampire to an inactive
vampire and have that vampire 'Hunt' to regain blood?
Also about Torpor, when a vampire is there how does he regain blood?
does it simply increase every turn?

And a general question about using cards. is the blood cost on them
payed by you blood counts or by the own vampire's assigned blood?

That's it for now, i'm sure i have more questions but i can't seem to
remember them now.

Thanks.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
cool....@gmail.com wrote:
> Hello,
> I have some questions about the game mechanics and rules i don't seem
> to understand, i hope someone here could help me out because i can't
> seem to find help anywhere else.
> I've got a few questions which follows:
>
> Action modifier cards: will using them Tap a minion?

No.
Things that tap a minion:

Attempting an action [6.2.1].
Blocking successfully [6.2.3].
Using the Slave ability [11].
Explicit card text.

That's all.

> Are they a one turn card which gets burned after using or are they
> permanent to the assigned minion?

One-use. Played to the ash heap. Unless card text explicitly says otherwise.

> The whole inactive region was also a little confusing, how much blood
> counts does it cost to bring a vampire from your crypt? how much does

Uh-oh. "Inactive region" is a term that hasn't been used in many years --
indicating you're probably using a very out-of-date rulebook.

Check the current rulebook here: http://www.white-wolf.com/vtes/rulebook/

To move a card from your crypt to your uncontrolled region, it costs 1 pool and
4 transfers.

See http://www.white-wolf.com/vtes/rulebook/rulebook.html#sec7

> it cost to bring a vampire into the active region and how much does it
> cost to move him back to the inactive region?

To move a vampire from your uncontrolled region, it costs an amount of pool
(paid one at a time via the use of transfers during one or more influence
phases) equal to the vampire's capacity.

There is no way to move a vampire back to the uncontrolled region (other than
explicit card text to do so).

> Can you move blood counts from an active vampire to an inactive
> vampire and have that vampire 'Hunt' to regain blood?

You cannot move blood from a ready vampire to anywhere (other than moving it to
the blood bank, that is: "burning" it, to pay blood cost or handle damage),
unless explicit card text tells you to.

> Also about Torpor, when a vampire is there how does he regain blood?

He doesn't (unless explicit card text says to). If he's empty, then he'll have
to be rescued -- he'll never have enough blood to leave torpor by himself.

> does it simply increase every turn?

No.

> And a general question about using cards. is the blood cost on them
> payed by you blood counts or by the own vampire's assigned blood?

You, the Methuselah, do not have blood -- you have pool.

The card's pool cost is paid from your pool.
The card's blood cost is paid from the vampire's blood.

http://www.white-wolf.com/vtes/rulebook/rulebook.html#sec1_6_1

Messages.Author: Jozxyqk
Messages.Body:
cool....@gmail.com wrote:
> Hello,
> I have some questions about the game mechanics and rules i don't seem
> to understand, i hope someone here could help me out because i can't
> seem to find help anywhere else.
> I've got a few questions which follows:

> Action modifier cards: will using them Tap a minion?

Most action modifier cards are played by a minion who is already tapped,
since you tap them to perform the action. But action modifiers do not
inherently tap a minion. For example, if an untapped minion plays a
superior Cloak the Gathering on another minion's action, the Cloaker
won't tap.

> Are they a one turn card which gets burned after using or are they
> permanent to the assigned minion?

One time.

> The whole inactive region was also a little confusing, how much blood
> counts does it cost to bring a vampire from your crypt?

During your influence phase, you have 4 Transfers. They are like a special
type of action.
It costs 4 Transfers, and one pool, to draw a vampire from your crypt into
the uncontrolled region.

> how much does
> it cost to bring a vampire into the active region?

It costs 1 transfer to move a blood from your pool to an uncontrolled vampire.
If the vampire has enough blood counters on him at the end of your influence
phase, then the vampire comes out into the ready region.

> and how much does it
> cost to move him back to the inactive region?

Why would you want to do that? It is usually an offensive action (like the
political action "Banishment") which would move a vampire back into the
uncontrolled region.

> Can you move blood counts from an active vampire to an inactive
> vampire and have that vampire 'Hunt' to regain blood?

You can't move blood from one vampire to another vampire without some
sort of explicit effect on a card (like Nikolaus Vermeulen or Saulot's
abilities).

> Also about Torpor, when a vampire is there how does he regain blood?

He doesn't, except if a card effect would allow it (like the Regeneration
action).

> does it simply increase every turn?

No.

> And a general question about using cards. is the blood cost on them
> payed by you blood counts or by the own vampire's assigned blood?

If there is a blood drop in the middle-left side of the card, or a red
blood drop on the bottom left (depending on the layout), then the vampire
pays the blood cost.

If there is a black blood drop in the bottom left, or a Skull-Diamond,
then you pay the cost from your own pool.

I hope this helps..

Messages.Author: Oortje
Messages.Body:
On 3 apr, 14:01, cool.ch...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hello,
> I have some questions about the game mechanics and rules i don't seem
> to understand, i hope someone here could help me out because i can't
> seem to find help anywhere else.
> I've got a few questions which follows:
>
> Action modifier cards: will using them Tap a minion?

No. Unless the card says so. example: Hidden lurker

> Are they a one turn card which gets burned after using or are they
> permanent to the assigned minion?

No they are burned. Unless the card says so like "spying Mission"
stays in play.

> The whole inactive region was also a little confusing, how much blood
> counts does it cost to bring a vampire from your crypt? how much does
> it cost to bring a vampire into the active region and how much does it
> cost to move him back to the inactive region?

Basicly each transfer phase gives you 4 transfers for that phase.
Transfers can be used as followed.
1 transfer: to move 1 blood from your pool to an inactive vampire
2 transfers: to move 1 blood from an inactive vampire to your pool
4 transfers: pay 1 pool to put the top vampire of your crypt to your
inactive region.
If (this is the cost) a vampire in your inactive region has blood
equal (or more, but this is not advisable) to his capacity (white
number in the lower right corner) at the end of your transfer phase,
that vampire is turned face up to the active region.
A vampire of capacity 8 will cost you 8 pool and 8 transfers, so it
needs 2 turns to be "transfer out"
Once a vampire is active it cannot be put back to your inactive
region.

> Can you move blood counts from an active vampire to an inactive
> vampire and have that vampire 'Hunt' to regain blood?

Some special abilities and cards allow you to put blood from active
vampires and even the bloodbank on uncontrolled vampires. A vampire
can normally not do that.

> Also about Torpor, when a vampire is there how does he regain blood?
> does it simply increase every turn?

A vampire in torpor does not and can not gain blood (except for some
specific card). A vampire needs to be ready in order to be able to
hunt. Torpor = not ready. So first you have to rescue the vampire,
before it can hunt.

> And a general question about using cards. is the blood cost on them
> payed by you blood counts or by the own vampire's assigned blood?

New cards have a RED blood drop for blood cost and a skull in a coffin
for pool cost.
Older cards have a BLACK blood drop for blood in the centre left for
blood cost and a BLACK blood drop in the lower left corner for pool
cost.

> That's it for now, i'm sure i have more questions but i can't seem to
> remember them now.
>
> Thanks.

I hope it helps a little,
Greetings,
Oortje

>>> And a general question about using cards. is the blood cost on them
>>> payed by you blood counts or by the own vampire's assigned blood?

>> blood drop on the bottom left (depending on the layout), then the vampire

> 'Blood Drop' illustration painted on the bottom left side of the card.

The old Jyhad cards used blood drops for both pool and blood costs.

Generally, the black numbers in a white drop meant blood cost. The white numbers
in a black drop meant pool cost. But at least one card had a misprint. The
position of the drop is always correct, however -- at the bottom means pool, in
the middle of the left side means blood.

The old Jyhad rulebook had that effect on a lot of players.
Hopefully the new one is clearer.

> About blocking and reaction cards:
> Reaction cards, when do you apply them? do you apply them whenever you
> want to block another Methuselah's move even if it's not your turn?

Yes. Reaction cards are played when another player is acting.

> and i assume these are one use cards as well? (which gets burned after
> usage)

Correct.

> Also about blocking, can you use any vampire at your disposal to block
> another vampire? or does the vampire have to be untapped?

Only untapped vampires can attempt to block (unless card text says otherwise).
Likewise, only untapped vampires can play reaction cards.

> As i understand it you can't block another vampire unless you have an
> 'Intercept' of above 0 (that is, equal to the other vampire's
> 'Stealth' or above it) and cannot block actions by default, which also
> means that since 'Bleed' has a default 'Stealth' of 1 it cannot be
> blocked.
> Is this right?

No. You've got the intercept vs. stealth part right, but not the default.

The default stealth of a bleed is zero, not 1.
So a minion with 0 intercept can block.

Hunting, equipping, recruiting allies, employing retainers, and calling
political actions all have a default of 1 stealth. But bleeding has a default of
zero. Other actions (from action cards) have a default of 0 unless the card text
says otherwise.

Aggravated Damage:

The first point of agg damage your vampire takes (so damage that is
not prevented via Fortitude, for example) sends your vampire to torpor
during the strike resolution phase. If only one point of agg damage is
taken, the vampire goes to torpor with no loss of blood. For each
additional point of agg damage a vampire takes, it must burn a blood,
the same as regular damage. If the vampire is unable to burn the
blood, then that vampire "burns" and is sent to the ash heap. Also,
it's worth noting that normal (non agg) damage is resolved before agg
damage. It is also worth noting that vampires burnt in this way does
not cause a blood hunt to be called, as long as the vampire burns from
sheer damage.

Blocking:

You are correct that you need an untaped minion to block (or play most
reaction cards for that matter) You can play cards that allow you to
block or play reaction cards "as if untapped" such as wake with
evenings freshness, forced awakening and On the Qui Vive in order to
allow your tapped minon to block the action in question. As far as
"getting out of combat", I'm not exactly sure what you mean. If you
mean "My vampire survived the combat" then it unaps in your round,
same as all of your other cards in play, at the beginning of your
untap phase. The only thing that can prevent this is having a card
used against you ( such as a flash grenade) which specificly prohibits
you from untapping. If you mean "get out of combat" by means of say,
majesty at superior, your vampire untaps as per the normal text of the
card and is quite free to attempt to block another action as the
vampire is now untapped.

Hope that helps some

Sutekh_23

Messages.Author: The Lasombra
Messages.Body:
On 7 Apr 2007 07:45:12 -0700, "cool....@gmail.com"
<cool....@gmail.com> wrote:

>Hey guys,
>I've got a few more questions about the game

Ok.

>Aggravated damage:
>How does this work exactly?

See section 3.2 of the FAQ.

http://www.thelasombra.com/vtes_faq.htm

3.2. How does aggravated damage work?

To burn a ready vampire with X blood, you must inflict X+2 damage, one
of which must be aggravated. Here's how that works:

* A vampire burns 1 blood to "heal" each point of normal damage
dealt to it. Note that "healing" damage is different from
"preventing" damage.
* A vampire is "wounded" if it has unhealed damage, is in torpor,
or is going to torpor.
* A vampire which cannot heal damage goes to torpor.
* A vampire cannot heal aggravated damage done to it.
* For each point of aggravated damage done to a wounded vampire,
that vampire must burn one blood to prevent destruction.
* A vampire which cannot prevent destruction is burned.

See also 6.4.6 of the online rulebook.

http://www.white-wolf.com/vtes/rulebook/

Some damage is described as aggravated damage, such as damage from
fire or sunlight or from the claws or fangs of some other immortal
creatures, including some vampires. Aggravated damage differs from
normal damage in two ways: Aggravated damage cannot be healed, and
aggravated damage can burn a vampire if that vampire is already
wounded. Aggravated damage is damage that a vampire cannot heal. Since
it cannot be healed, the vampire doesn't burn any blood to heal it,
but instead becomes wounded (unless the damage is prevented, of
course).

Aggravated damage done to a wounded vampire can burn the vampire
outright. A wounded vampire is one that has taken damage that he
failed to heal or one that is in torpor or on his way to torpor. For
each point of aggravated damage that is successfully inflicted on a
wounded vampire, he must burn a blood to prevent his destruction. If
he doesn't have enough blood, he is burned. Destruction by this method
does not constitute diablerie (see Diablerie, sec. 6.5.5).

If both regular damage and aggravated damage are successfully
inflicted on a vampire at the same time, the regular damage is handled
first. This only applies to unprevented damage; damage prevention
effects can be used to prevent the aggravated damage before the normal
damage, if the player chooses. If a vampire is wounded, he goes to
torpor after all the damage is handled (see Torpor, sec. 6.5). If
aggravated damage burns him, he goes directly to the ash heap. He
doesn’t go through torpor first.

>as i get it the vampire is burned if
>inflicted aggravated damage twice in the same combat? (not in the same
>round put possible)

In general, no.
See specifics above.

>And also a fairly simple question.
>As i understand you need an untapped minion to preform a block, but if
>you succeed in blocking and get out of combat, does the minion stay
>tapped in the next round?

No.

See section 4 of the online rulebook.

http://www.white-wolf.com/vtes/rulebook/

At the beginning of your untap phase, you must untap all of your
cards. Any cards or effects that require or allow you to do something
during your untap phase take effect after you have untapped your
cards.

Carpe noctem.

Lasombra

http://www.TheLasombra.com

Your best online source for information about V:TES.
Now also featuring individual card sales and sales
of booster and starter box displays.

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <1175959704.5...@b75g2000hsg.googlegroups.com>,

sutekh_23 <bec...@aapt.net.au> writes:
>Aggravated Damage:
>
>The first point of agg damage your vampire takes (so damage that is
>not prevented via Fortitude, for example) sends your vampire to torpor
>during the strike resolution phase.

This is misleading. If the agg damage is taken at a different point in
combat (for example, Weather Control during a Dawn Operation), the
vampire will go to torpor during the resolution of that damage, assuming
it is unprevented etc.

> If only one point of agg damage is
>taken, the vampire goes to torpor with no loss of blood. For each
>additional point of agg damage a vampire takes, it must burn a blood,
>the same as regular damage.

This ("the same as regular damage") is also misleading.

The vampire burns blood to prevent destruction once they are wounded.
They heal damage when unwounded. The difference is important for a
small number of cards. For example:

- Regenerative Blood will allow an unwounded vampire to burn 1 blood and
heal 2 damage. It will not allow a vampire to burn 1 blood for
2 points of damage that will cause their destruction.

- Sword of Nuln requires twice as much blood to heal, but not to prevent
destruction.

These two things are not the same.

Messages.Author: The Lasombra
Messages.Body:
On 8 Apr 2007 09:25:27 -0700, "cool....@gmail.com"
<cool....@gmail.com> wrote:

>I'm still a little confused here.
>Just to clear things up a bit, i'm using the first edition deck.
>As i understand it a vampire goes to torpor once he has taken damage
>that he cannot pay for (via the bloodcounts that is).

Correct. That is the primary (or most frequent) way that a vampire
will enter torpor.

>How exactly does aggravated damage come into play here?

Aggravated damage is completely separate from this.

A single point of aggravated damage will send a vampire to torpor,
whether or not they have any blood counters left.

Two points of aggravated damage taken with the vampire has no blood
counters left will burn the vampire.

If a vampire is going to torpor taking more damage then it has blood,
and there is still a point of aggravated damage left to be handled,
then that point of damage will burn the vampire.

Aggravated damage is pretty rare in the Jyhad set.

Body of Sun (R)
Burst of Sunlight (R)
Claws of the Dead (C)
Dawn Operation (U)
Dragon's Breath Rounds (U)
Flamethrower (U)
Ivory Bow (R)
Sengir Dagger (R)
Walk of Flame (U)
Wolf Claws (C)

You are most likely to run into Claws of the Dead and Wolf Claws, so
you will only infrequently have to deal with more than 1 point of
aggravated damage.

Always completely resolve all of the non-aggravated damage first, if
damage is coming from two sources at the same time. (i.e. Wolf
Companion + hand strike)

Carpe noctem.

Lasombra

Messages.Author: Janne Hägglund
Messages.Body:
"cool....@gmail.com" <cool....@gmail.com> writes:

I once read an insanely elegant description of how aggravated damage works.
It has three steps:

1) A point of normal damage makes your vampire burn a blood.
If he can't burn a blood, he goes to torpor.

2) A point of aggravated damage makes your vampire go to torpor.
If he can't go to torpor, he burns a blood.

3) If your vampire can't go to torpor and can't burn a blood,
then a point of aggravated damage will burn him.

(Clarification: "Can't go to torpor," because he's already going to torpor.)

That's correct. Remember, Methuselah = player, so if a card says some
Methuselah has to show every other Methuselah her hand, that means
that player has to show every other player the cards in her hand. In
the case of Owl Companion, "open hand" means the Methuselah
[controlling a minion which is in combat opposing a minion with an Owl
Companion] must play with her hand face-up on the table so all the
other players can see what's in her hand, including draws and
redraws.

Messages.Author: John Flournoy
Messages.Body:
On Apr 23, 10:34 am, "cool.ch...@gmail.com" <cool.ch...@gmail.com>
wrote:

> Hello everyone,
> I am now looking to buy cards from a newer edition
>
> On Apr 3, 7:00 am, Jozxyqk <jfeue...@eecs.tufts.edu> wrote:
>
> >; most
> > cards are still legal (even from Jyhad), and most players are willing
> > to teachnewplayers as well.
>
> is that true?
> If i own decks from both the first edition and the third edition, will
> i be able to combine decks?

Yes. Cards from any and every set can be mixed freely as you like (and
as your deck size permits.) The rulebook deck limits are:

Minimum Crypt: 12. No maximum.
Minimum Library: 40. Maximum: 40+10/player.

Most groups prefer to play with the 'tournament rule' deck size:
Library min 60, max 90.

> Which cards are deemed banned after the first edition was printed?

No card has been outright banned. A very short list of cards has been
banned from tournament play:

* Dramatic Upheaval (V:TES)
* Kindred Restructure (V:TES)
* Madness of the Bard (Dark Sovereigns)
* The Return to Innocence (Ancient Hearts)
* Succubus Club (V:TES)
* Any cards that are usable only when playing for ante, including:
o Cunctator Motion (V:TES)
o High Stakes (V:TES)
o Playing for Keeps (Dark Sovereigns)

That's it.

> also, what are all these special editions? (for example the 'legacies
> of blood' series, are they the same cards or a unique line?)

Different expansions add new library and crypt cards, including new
disciplines and clans/bloodlines. The following sets are 'core sets'
that are larger sets and include plenty of the more straightforward
cards that you'd want in starting a collection:

Jyhad/Vampire
Sabbat
Sabbat War
Camarilla
3rd Edition

Pretty much all of the starter decks focused on a single clan include
a number of these generically useful cards; players can build solid
decks by combining the contents of a couple of starter decks with a
few appropriate boosters. It's also worth noting that the contents of
all the starter decks after Jyhad/Vampire are not random but fixed -
every Toreador starter from Camarilla contains the same set of cards.

> What kind of balance problems can i expect when combining decks?

Starter decks from different sets might not have much in common; for
instance a Camarilla Malkavian starter has almost nothing in common
with the Legacies of Blood Ishtarri starter - the vampires within are
of different sects, different clans, and use different disciplines. So
the non-generic library cards in each deck usually won't be playable
by the crypt cards in the other, making it hard to build a coherent
deck out of the two.

It's generally much better to combine from decks that have some
overlap - the same clan, sect, and/or some of the same disciplines.

It's also worth making sure that the boosters that you acquire are
from sets that contain a similar focus to the deck(s) you're building.

For instance, a single Final Nights booster won't be of much use to
you if all your cards are Jyhad-set - FN focuses on clans and sects
and disciplines that you don't already have, so that one booster will
mostly have cards you can't yet use without more of that set.

> Thanks.

-John Flournoy

Messages.Author: witness1
Messages.Body:
On Apr 23, 11:34 am, "cool.ch...@gmail.com" <cool.ch...@gmail.com>

>
> >; most
> > cards are still legal (even from Jyhad), and most players are willing
> > to teachnewplayers as well.
>
> is that true?
> If i own decks from both the first edition and the third edition, will
> i be able to combine decks?

There is a caveat: the grouping rule. Newer vampires (since Camarilla
Edition) have a small white number printed on their lower left corner.
Cards printed prior to Cam Ed are group 1 (if they are from Jyhad/
V:tES base set - i.e., have no expansion symbol) or group 2 (if they
are from any other expansion). You are only allowed to use two
consecutive groups when constructing your deck (i.e., groups 1 and 2
together, or groups 2 and 3 together, but not 1 and 3 together, and
not 1, 2, and 3 together).

Note that two players with different grouping pairs can still play
against each other - the grouping rule only applies to deck
construction.

> Which cards are deemed banned after the first edition was printed?

The following cards are banned in all V:EKN tournaments:

Dramatic Upheaval (V:TES)
Kindred Restructure (V:TES)

Madness of the Bard (Dark Sovereigns)

The Return to Innocence (Ancient Hearts)

Succubus Club (V:TES)

Any cards that are usable only when playing for ante, including:

Cunctator Motion (V:TES)
High Stakes (V:TES)

Playing for Keeps (Dark Sovereigns)

> also, what are all these special editions? (for example the 'legacies

> of blood' series, are they the same cards or a unique line?)

Legacies of Blood is an expansion much like any other. It introduced
four new clans and one new discipline, as well as new vampires and
library cards for the various bloodlines previously released.

> What kind of balance problems can i expect when combining decks?

You should find that most well-built decks hold up fairly well against
the newer competition, and it will hopefully not be an issue. There
will probably be some new cards that would improve your deck, but all-
Jyhad decks still come up every once in a while and still do ok.

> Thanks.

You're welcome!

witness1

> > to teachnewplayers as well.
>
> is that true?

Yes, Every single card every printed for VTES is legal barring the
following list of 8 cards.

The following cards are banned in all V:EKN tournaments:

* Dramatic Upheaval (V:TES)

* Kindred Restructure (V:TES)
* Madness of the Bard (Dark Sovereigns)
* The Return to Innocence (Ancient Hearts)
* Succubus Club (V:TES)
* Any cards that are usable only when playing for ante, including:
o Cunctator Motion (V:TES)
o High Stakes (V:TES)

o Playing for Keeps (Dark Sovereigns)

> If i own decks from both the first edition and the third edition, will
> i be able to combine decks?

The library cards you can combine freely, but the vampires are now
grouped. Only vampires from adjacent groups are compatable (i.e. 1+2,
2+3, 3+4, 4+5).

Vampire Grouping is determined by the following rule.

Group: Each vampire belongs to a specific group, identified by a
number above the upper left corner of the text box. A player's crypt
must be built using vampires from a single group or from two
consecutive groups. This does not restrict a Methuselah from stealing
vampires from other groups through play, however. Cards from some
older sets do not have this designation. For those cards, the ones
with an expansion set symbol (an icon in the upper right corner of the
card) are treated as Group 2 vampires; the others are Group 1
vampires.

> Which cards are deemed banned after the first edition was printed?

The following cards are banned in all V:EKN tournaments:

* Dramatic Upheaval (V:TES)

* Kindred Restructure (V:TES)
* Madness of the Bard (Dark Sovereigns)
* The Return to Innocence (Ancient Hearts)
* Succubus Club (V:TES)
* Any cards that are usable only when playing for ante, including:
o Cunctator Motion (V:TES)
o High Stakes (V:TES)

o Playing for Keeps (Dark Sovereigns)

> also, what are all these special editions? (for example the 'legacies
> of blood' series, are they the same cards or a unique line?)

Each expansion or "special edition" as you call them introduces a new
facet to the game. They are playable on there own or in combonation
with other sets.

> What kind of balance problems can i expect when combining decks?

The game is balanced, just make sure you have a legal crypt.

Welcome back to the game. :)

Comments Welcome,
Norman S. Brown, Jr
XZealot
Archon of the Swamp

>

I'd like to clarify, and point out that the grouping rule only applies to
crypt cards (orange backs). Library cards (green backs) can be freely mixed
between sets and editions.

So in your example, where you had cards from the first edition (Jyhad/VTES)
and third edition, all your vampires would have to come from either only
first or only third edition, but you can freely use any non-vampire cards you
like.

[Snip question about banned cards, I have nothing to add]

> > also, what are all these special editions? (for example the 'legacies
> > of blood' series, are they the same cards or a unique line?)
>
> Legacies of Blood is an expansion much like any other. It introduced
> four new clans and one new discipline, as well as new vampires and
> library cards for the various bloodlines previously released.

One good thing to know is the difference between base sets and expansions.

Base sets, such as third edition, are designed to be everything you need.
That means if you buy third edition boosters, and nothing else at all, you
can still create lots of cool and viable decks.

Base sets are Jyhad, VTES, Sabbat, Sabbat War, Camarilla Edition and
Third Edition.

>
> > What kind of balance problems can i expect when combining decks?
>
> You should find that most well-built decks hold up fairly well against
> the newer competition, and it will hopefully not be an issue. There
> will probably be some new cards that would improve your deck, but all-
> Jyhad decks still come up every once in a while and still do ok.

You don't need to own cards from different sets, but it would do you good to
*know* the most important cards from different sets. That way you'll get
less nasty surprises. "Hmm, he has lots of little Ravnos, but they can only
bleed for one, so I should be safe. Hey, what's that card?"

HG

Messages.Author: Salem
Messages.Body:


effectively, but not really the correct reasoning.

The edition of the cards has no bearing whatsoever on whether or not you
can mix them. All editions are freely mixable within the one deck with
all other editions (and playable against other decks made with any
editions).

However, the *grouping rule* prevents mixing crypt cards that are not of
consecutive groups within a given crypt, and it just so happens that 3rd
edition crypt cards are all 2 or more groups ahead of jyhad edition
crypt cards.

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
On Apr 23, 10:36 pm, "cool.ch...@gmail.com" <cool.ch...@gmail.com>
wrote:

> Lets take that literaly.
> Say i have a first edition JYHAD starter deck and am acquiring third
> edition booster packs and nothing else at all.
> I will still be able to combine JYHAD starter deck library cards with
> third edition booster packs yet crypt cards would have to be of the
> same edition.
>
> Is this right?

Yes. Granted, a lot of the Jyhad cards have slightly different wording
than the 3rd Ed cards (in any situation where your Jyhad cards have
different wording than your 3rd cards, the 3rd wording is correct).
And as noted, the vampire groups don't mix (Jyhad vampires are Group
1; 3rd vampires are Group 4; you can only mix vampires of 2 adjacent
groups, i.e. 1/2 or 2/3 or 3/4), but if you are playing with a limited
pool of cards, it is pretty safe to ignore the grouping rule till you
get more cards (unless you are playing in a tournament).

But the short answer is: Yes, you can freely mix Jyhad, VTES, 3rd,
whatever cards together in your decks.

-Peter
